content:
Wednesday is confirmed as a returning series on Netflix, with Jenna Ortega back at Nevermore Academy.

Here's what's confirmed, and why a show that should have been a one-note gimmick keeps working.

DetailInfo
StarringJenna Ortega, Steve Buscemi, Emma Myers, Hunter Doohan
PlatformNetflix
Seasons3 · 16 episodes
StatusReturning Series
TMDB rating4.2 / 5

Where the Show Stands

Sixteen episodes across three seasons, holding a 4.2/5 TMDB rating — strong for a show built on a character who has existed since a 1960s sitcom.

The premise remains simple. Wednesday Addams is enrolled at Nevermore Academy, a school for outcasts, where she investigates supernatural mysteries while making almost no effort to be liked.

The confirmed cast now includes Steve Buscemi, whose presence signals something about the register the show is aiming for — he is very good at characters whose authority is undercut by visible unease.

Alongside him: Emma Myers as Enid, Hunter Doohan as Tyler, Joy Sunday as Bianca, plus Moosa Mostafa, Georgie Farmer and Isaac Ordonez as Pugsley.

Why Jenna Ortega's Performance Carries It

Playing Wednesday is harder than it looks, and the difficulty is specific: the character has almost no facial expression and no tonal variation.

That means everything has to be carried by timing, stillness and physicality. Ortega plays her as genuinely unbothered rather than performing detachment — which is the difference between the character being funny and being irritating.

She has also spoken publicly about pushing back on lines and scenes she felt broke the character, particularly anything that made Wednesday warmer or more conventionally likeable. That kind of protectiveness usually shows up on screen, and here it does.

The dance sequence from Season 1 became a genuine cultural moment, and it's worth noting she choreographed it herself. Almost none of the show's most-shared images come from the plot.

Why the Show Works Better Than It Should

On paper this is a franchise-extension gimmick — a decades-old side character given her own teen mystery series. Most of those fail.

Three reasons it doesn't:

It commits to the joke. Wednesday is never softened into a misunderstood teen with a heart of gold. The show resists the obvious arc, and that restraint is why the small moments of connection land at all.

The mystery is real. The plotting is a functioning whodunnit rather than an excuse to hang character moments on. You can actually follow the clues.

The production design does heavy lifting. Nevermore is a genuinely realized place, and the visual identity is strong enough to survive being screenshotted endlessly.

The Honest Criticism

The weakest element has been the supporting students, who periodically flatten into archetypes — the bubbly roommate, the moody love interest, the mean popular girl.

The show also leans hard on the teen-drama scaffolding it's simultaneously mocking. Season to season, how much of that it can carry without becoming the thing it satirises is the open question.

Season 3 will likely be judged on whether the ensemble gets the depth Ortega's lead has had from the start.

Where to Watch

All seasons stream on Netflix. Season 1 is 8 episodes and works as a self-contained mystery — a good test of whether the tone is for you before committing further.
